117927.name: Lubavitch Jewish Center of Alaska
117927.note: Jewish Press: 'when Rabbi Yosef and Esther Greenberg arrived in Alaska in 1991 they set up the Chabad-Lubavitch Jewish Center of Alaska'; J. Weekly: they arrived in Anchorage in 1991 as newlyweds to set up Alaska's first Chabad center; a 1999 Detroit Jewish News item: established in 1991. (One profile says 1990.) lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Aug 24 2011 lists it at 1210 East 26th Avenue, Anchorage; it is now at 1117 East 35th Avenue, so it moved after 2011 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 1210 East 26th Avenue, Anchorage (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Aug 24 2011)

118662.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Idaho
118662.note: Its About page: 'Rabbi & Mrs. Lifshitz moved to Boise in April 2004 to establish Chabad Lubavitch of Idaho'; the Idaho Statesman, 5 Dec 2004, on their arrival (jewishidaho.com/Article.asp?AID=239998). The first Chabad shluchim in Idaho. lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009 lists it at 8707 W. State St., Boise; it is now at 1803 S Maple Grove Road, so it moved after 2009 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 8707 W. State St., Boise (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009)

486805.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Montana
486805.note: CrownHeights.info, 13 Mar 2007 (from the Bozeman press): 'A Jewish rabbi is moving here'; Chaim and Chavie Bruk 'intend to set up a base in Bozeman'. J. (Aug 2009): the Bruks 'arrived in Bozeman in early 2007'. Lubavitch.com (Feb 2022) says 'since arriving in Bozeman in 2006' (his first visit). The first permanent Chabad center in Montana. lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Aug 30 2011 lists it at 8755 Huffman Lane, Bozeman; it is now at 1610 Ellis Street Suite 2B, so it moved after 2011 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 8755 Huffman Lane, Bozeman (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Aug 30 2011)

117787.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Alberta
117787.note: The Jewish Historical Society of Southern Alberta's description of its archive: Chabad became a full-time presence in Calgary in 1988 with the arrival of Rabbi Menachem and Rochel Matusof; its emissaries first came in 1981 to run a summer day camp. Its own site and a CrownHeights.info profile give 1988; one Lubavitch.com piece says 1986. lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Aug 29 2011 lists it at 523 Woodpark Blvd. SW #28, Calgary; it is now at 134 Forge Road SE, so it moved after 2011 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 523 Woodpark Blvd. SW #28, Calgary (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Aug 29 2011)

117898.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Edmonton
117898.note: Alberta Jewish News, 6 Jan 2017: Chabad 'celebrated their twenty-fifth anniversary as part of the Jewish Community of Edmonton' (Dec 2016), 'the twenty-five years since Rabbi Ari arrived'; a community directory: 'since its founding in 1991 ... led by Rabbi Ari Drelich'. (The Alberta archive says an Edmonton branch opened in 1990; another listing says 1992.) lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009 lists it at 84 Westridge Road, Edmonton; it is now at 502 Wolf Willow Road nw, so it moved after 2009 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 84 Westridge Road, Edmonton (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009)

117790.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of the Maritimes
117790.note: 24 Jan 2008: 'Thirteen years ago, Chabad representatives Rabbi Mendel and Bassie Feldman and one month old Zevi moved to Halifax to stay.' Anash.org: shluchim in Halifax 'since 5755 (1995), when they established Chabad Lubavitch of the Maritimes' (5755 = autumn 1994 to summer 1995). lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009 lists it at 5595 Fenwick Street, Halifax; it is now at 1171 Waterloo Street, so it moved after 2009 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 5595 Fenwick Street, Halifax (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009)

118602.name: Chabad at Dartmouth
118602.note: The Dartmouth, Sept 2003: 'Chabad Lubavitchers open Hanover center' (Moshe and Chani Gray, from Brooklyn, that fall); Dartmouth Alumni Magazine: 'founded in the fall of 2003 by Moshe and Chani Gray'. lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009 lists it at 22A School Street, Hanover; it is now at 19 Allen Street, so it moved after 2009 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 22A School Street, Hanover (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009)

117608.name: Chabad of Hawaii
117608.note: Chabad.org, 18 Nov 2007: Rabbi Itchel and Pearl Krasnjansky 'arrived in August 1987 with a toddler'; 'the culmination of 20 years of Chabad-Lubavitch activities in Hawaii'. The Star-Bulletin (2001): they moved from New York about 14 years before. lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009 lists it at 410 Atkinson Drive, the Ala Moana Hotel, Honolulu; it is now at 2241 Kapiolani Blvd 6th Floor, so it moved after 2009 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 410 Atkinson Drive, the Ala Moana Hotel, Honolulu (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009)

117652.name: Chabad of New Hampshire
117652.note: 'Chabad Lubavitch of New Hampshire, founded in 1989'; the Krinskys 'have been based out of central Manchester since 1989'. The state's first Chabad house. lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Aug 31 2011 lists it at 7 Camelot Place, Manchester; it is now at 1234 River Road, so it moved after 2011 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 7 Camelot Place, Manchester (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Aug 31 2011)

582611.name: Rohr Chabad House at Vanderbilt
582611.note: Lubavitch.com (24 Oct 2007, via CrownHeights.info): 'Chabad Opens Student Center At Vanderbilt University', Rabbi Shlomo and Nechama Rothstein its new representatives (comments: 'finally its official', 'we can't wait for you to come'). The Jewish Observer (Dec 2024): they began 17 years ago. lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009 lists it at 436 Village at Vanderbilt, Nashville; it is now at 111 23rd Ave North, so it moved after 2009 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 436 Village at Vanderbilt, Nashville (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009)

767854.name: Monsey Beis Chaya Mushka High
767854.note: CrownHeights.info, Jan 26 2011 ('Monsey Beis Chaya Mushka Celebrates Third Dinner'): 'Monsey Beis Chaya Mushka High School for Girls opened in September of 2006 and has grown to almost 60 students'. (therebbesimpact.com: 2008.) Found by Firecrawl's research agent; the quote checked on the page. lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Sept 7 2011 lists it at 315 North Main Street, New City (Chabad of Rockland's address); it is now at 27 South Monsey Road, so it moved after 2011 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 315 North Main Street, New City (Chabad of Rockland's address) (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Sept 7 2011)

118273.name: Chabad Community Center For Jewish Life and Learning
118273.note: Lubavitch.com, 22 May 2019: 'When Rabbi Ovadia and Nechoma Goldman came to town in 1998, they were told Oklahoma City was reform country.' (Another Chabad report calls them founders in 1997.) First called Chabad of Oklahoma City. lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Aug 31 2011 lists it at 3016 Castlerock Road, Oklahoma City (as Chabad of Oklahoma City); it is now at 3000 W Hefner Road, so it moved after 2011 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 3016 Castlerock Road, Oklahoma City (as Chabad of Oklahoma City) (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Aug 31 2011)

117638.name: Chabad Lubavitch of Maine
117638.note: Its staff page: 'He arrived in Portland, Maine together with his wife Chana in 1987'; a Portland Press Herald piece by his son and a 2019 travel article ('since 1987') agree. lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Aug 30 2011 lists it at 101 Craigie Street, Portland; it is now at 11 Pomeroy street, so it moved after 2011 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 101 Craigie Street, Portland (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Aug 30 2011)

117789.name: Chabad-Lubavitch of Winnipeg
117789.note: Its own Historical Outline of Growth: '1972: Lubavitch Centre established in Winnipeg by Rabbi A. Altein.' The CJN (13 July 2026): Rabbi Avrohom and Brocha Altein 'moved to Winnipeg in 1972'. (The same outline: South End branch on Grant Avenue 1994; Jewish Learning Centre on Mathers Avenue built from 2010, opened Chanukah 2011.) lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009 lists it at 2095 Sinclair Street, Winnipeg (the Lubavitch Centre of Winnipeg, North End); its listing is now at 1845 Mathers Avenue, the Jewish Learning Centre that its own outline says opened Chanukah 2011 (the Chabad Jewish Learning Institute was at 901 Shaftesbury Blvd. in 2009).

earlier.where: 2095 Sinclair Street, Winnipeg (the Lubavitch Centre of Winnipeg, North End) (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009)

677505.name: Rohr Chabad Student Network of Ottawa
677505.note: Rabbi Chaim and Yocheved Boyarsky established the Rohr Chabad Student Network of Ottawa in 2008 (COLlive; Chabad.org: they have directed it 'since 2008'), first in their home; later the Finkelstein downtown center. lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Aug 30 2011 lists it at 29 Gilmour Street, Ottawa; it is now at 254 Friel Street, so it moved after 2011 (when, not found).

earlier.where: the Boyarskys' home
29 Gilmour Street, Ottawa (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Aug 30 2011)

118578.name: Cheder Chabad of Monsey
118578.note: Monsey (no shetach). Private School Review: founded 1999; GuideStar's IRS ruling year 2001; therebbesimpact.com: 1999. Rabbi Yisroel Shusterman, dean; its modular building in Airmont went up in 2012 (Lubavitch.com, Nov 2012); a five-acre New City campus bought later. Checked (Nov 7): its own site (https://www.chedermonsey.org/): 'Established in 1999 by Rabbi & Mrs. [Shusterman]', so high. lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009 lists it at 58 Parker Boulevard, Monsey (its boys' division; the school itself listed at P.O. Box 1164); it is now at 15 Widman Court, so it moved after 2009 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 58 Parker Boulevard, Monsey (its boys' division; the school itself listed at P.O. Box 1164) (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009)

705397.name: Chabad of Taos
705397.note: The Canadian Jewish News, Jan 17 2020 (Sandy Bornstein, 'The remote Jews of Taos, N.M.'): 'Chabad has had a presence in Taos since 2008.' (Rabbi Eliyahu and Batsheva Kaminetzky; therebbesimpact.com and the listing number also point to 2008.) Found by Firecrawl's research agent; the quote checked on the page. lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Sept 7 2011 lists it at 208 Paseo del Canon East, Suite C, Taos; it is now at 221 Paseo del Pueblo Norte, so it moved after 2011 (when, not found).

earlier.where: 208 Paseo del Canon East, Suite C, Taos (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Sept 7 2011)

559424.name: Chabad of Kanata
559424.note: Ottawa Jewish Bulletin (about 2021, 'Russian-speaking Jews more engaged with community thanks to Genesis grant'): 'Gershzon said in 2005, the "Acheinu Board" was established to address the growing needs of a Russian-speaking Jewish population, which eventually led to the development of the Chabad of Kanata by bringing Rabbi Gershzon to Ottawa', so after 2005 (https://www.ottawajewishbulletin.com/jewish-ottawa/russian-speaking-jews-more-engaged-with-community-thanks-to-genesis-grant). The Chesed Fund (undated): the Gershzons 'founded Chabad of Kanata almost two decades ago'. therebbesimpact.com and the listing number point to 2007 (leads). Its chabad.org listing went up on Sep 16 2007 (chabad.org's own record), so it existed by then. It began as the Jewish Russian Community Centre of Ottawa (JRCC Ottawa): its site, archived June 16 2008 (copyright 2007), names Rabbi Michoel Gershzon, regional director, and Mrs. Miriam Gershzon (https://web.archive.org/web/20080616173605/http://www.jrccottawa.org/), and lubavitch.com's directory as archived Aug 30 2011 lists the Jewish Russian Community Center of Ottawa at 15 Hansen Ave. (Kanata). Neither gives a founding year.

earlier.where: 15 Hansen Ave., Kanata, as the Jewish Russian Community Centre of Ottawa (JRCC Ottawa; its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Aug 30 2011)

117621.name: Chabad of Kentucky
117621.note: Jewish Louisville, 'Chabad at 30' (22 Jan 2015): 'In March of 1985, Rabbi Avrohom and Goldie Litvin moved to Louisville' to open Chabad's branch for Kentucky; their first program was a Purim talk on the day they arrived. Its site: 'since 1985'. Its Chabad House on Almara Circle burned down in April 2022. lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009 lists Chabad of Kentucky (Rabbi Avrohom Litvin) at 3706 Dutchmans Lane.

earlier.where: the Chabad House on Almara Circle (burned down April 2022)
3706 Dutchmans Lane, Louisville (its address in lubavitch.com's center directory as archived Dec 28 2009)
